original_question: Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, Open Problem 5: prove Conjecture 1 for point visibility graphs with ω(G)=5, where Conjecture 1 asks for a function f such that χ(G)≤f(ω(G)).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the unresolved clique-number-5 case for point visibility graphs, uses the right invariants χ(G) and ω(G), and asks for an absolute bound on chromatic number independent of the particular graph. This matches the paper’s narrow surviving case after the discussion of ω(G)≤4 and the counterexample threshold at ω(G)=6.
missing_details: It should specify that G is the point visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane R^2.
It should define adjacency: vertices correspond to points of P, and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the line segment joining the corresponding points contains no other point of P.
It should make explicit that χ(G) is the proper vertex chromatic number and ω(G) is the clique number.
It should state that the constant c is universal, i.e. independent of the choice of P and G.
It should make clear that no general-position assumption is intended; collinearities are allowed.
To be paper-faithful, it should be tied explicitly to Open Problem 5, namely Conjecture 1 specialized to the case ω(G)=5.
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c such that for every finite point set P⊂R^2, if G is the point visibility graph of P (that is, V(G)=P and two vertices p,q∈P are adjacent exactly when the line segment pq contains no other point of P) and ω(G)=5, then χ(G)≤c?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s intended target. In Section 2.2 the paper states Conjecture 1, namely that point visibility graphs should satisfy χ(G)≤f(ω(G)) for some function f. Open Problem 5 then isolates the exact remaining bounded case ω(G)=5. This is the nearest official formulation to your draft. It should not be broadened to the full conjecture, nor shifted to the neighboring Open Problem 4 about ω(G)≤4. The surrounding context also explains why ω=5 is the sharp unresolved case in this discussion: the paper notes bounded behavior for small clique number and then records Pfender’s lemma showing that no such χ-bound can hold once ω(G) reaches 6.
